episode.title: A Fissure Opening Along the San Andreas

synopsis: An impossibly deep and wide fissure tears open along the San Andreas Fault, rending the California landscape apart and severing major highways as the chasm rapidly expands.

shots.prompt:

caption:
An impossibly wide and deep fissure tears open along the San Andreas Fault across the California landscape, USA.

The chasm is over 500 meters wide and kilometers deep, rapidly expanding as it severs major highways and consumes the terrain. Its raw, exposed rock walls glitter in the sun.

The San Andreas Fault is a transform fault where plates slide past each other, causing earthquakes, not gaping chasms. Surface ruptures are typically a few meters wide, like the 1906 San Francisco earthquake's offset of up to 6 meters.

Earth's crust is not brittle enough to sustain such an open void; gravity and lithostatic pressure would immediately cause the walls to collapse. The energy needed to instantaneously separate such a massive volume of rock and keep it open would far exceed the planet's tectonic forces.

This is a simulation, not real footage.

What other landscape features would vanish into such a rift?
